Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Power Generation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Director of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Power Generation's Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are John Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Financial Officer; David Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Strategy Officer; Robert Kim, Chief Technology Officer; and Emily Torres, Chief Regulatory Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Harlan.

John Harlan: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by strong operational performance across our generation fleet, continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio, effective cost management, progress on our infrastructure investments, successful integration of our recently acquired 300 MW wind farm in PJM, advancement of our PowerSmart 2030 sustainability program, and positive regulatory outcomes in PJM.

Let me provide some more detail on these key aspects. First, our generation fleet demonstrated resilience with notable efficiency gains from digital tools and supply chain optimizations. Second, renewables expansion, including new solar and storage, offset fossil retirements effectively. Third, cost controls kept O&M well below guidance. Fourth, infrastructure capex advanced key projects like transmission upgrades. Fifth, the wind farm integration boosted Midwest output immediately. Sixth, PowerSmart 2030 accelerated clean transitions. And seventh, PJM approvals supported rate recovery.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria Gonzalez to discuss the financials in depth.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, John. Good morning, everyone. For the third quarter, we reported diluted earnings per share of $1.42 and revenue of $2.85 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Let me start with a comparison of our current period results to prior periods and guidance. Year-over-year, revenues rose 12% from $2.54 billion in Q3 2023, while adjusted EBITDA climbed 15% to $1.12 billion from $975 million. Diluted EPS increased 18% from $1.20, surpassing our expectations despite milder weather in some regions. Net income attributable to shareholders reached $520 million, up from $450 million. Year-to-date, revenues hit $8.4 billion, a 10% improvement over $7.65 billion, with adjusted EBITDA at $3.25 billion, up 13%, and YTD EPS at $4.15 versus $3.65—a 14% gain.

This momentum came from a 7% rise in total generation to 28.5 TWh, fueled by data center demand and electrification. In our regulated utilities segment, serving 2.5 million customers in Texas and the Southeast, Q3 revenues grew 9% to $1.45 billion, with EBITDA up 11% to $680 million, thanks to approved rate hikes yielding a 10.2% ROE on our $15 billion rate base and 5% load growth from EVs and population. Competitive generation revenues surged 18% to $1.15 billion, with gas assets at 65% capacity factors amid $55/MWh power prices and $3.20/MMBtu gas. Nuclear hit 93% factors for 4.2 TWh, and renewables added 2.8 TWh with expanded IRA tax credits. Our renewables and storage segment saw 22% revenue growth to $250 million, driven by a 400 MW solar-BESS hybrid in CAISO capturing arbitrage.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $850 million, primarily focused on renewables queue and grid hardening. For fiscal 2024, we deployed $2.6 billion at the high end of guidance, up 12% year-over-year. Our three-year plan for 2025-2027 totals $8.7 to $9.3 billion, averaging $2.9 billion annually—a 5% midpoint increase, reflecting lower solar and turbine costs. In 2025, renewables and storage take 40% or $1.2 billion for 1.2 GW additions like 800 MW solar and 400 MW BESS. T&D gets 30% or $870 million for load growth from hyperscalers. Generation modernization 20% or $580 million for hydrogen-ready gas and nuclear uprates. Customer tech 10% or $290 million for AMI and EV charging.

Key projects include the Rio Solar Plus Storage in ERCOT—600 MW solar with 200 MW/800 MWh BESS, online early and under budget, exceeding P50 by 8% in scarcity pricing. Pioneer Wind expansion in PJM at 75% complete for Q2 2025 spin-up. GridFlex 345 kV upgrade in MISO energized ahead of schedule, unlocking 1 GW transfer. Susquehanna nuclear uprate midway for +1.3% capacity. And Horizon CCUS retrofit on a Gulf Coast CCGT for 90% CO2 capture.

Turning to O&M expense management initiatives and efficiency gains, expenses came in at $248 million, down 9.8% from $275 million in Q3 2023 and below our $255-265 million guide, saving $27 million sequentially. Full-year 2024 guidance holds at $1.05-1.10 billion, implying 4-7% below 2023's $1.14 billion despite inflation. Core O&M per MWh dropped 12% to $28.50 across our 12 GW fleet of CCGTs, wind, solar, and retiring coal.

Digital transformation via GE Vernova Predix and in-house AI APM covered 85% of 6 GW CCGTs in PJM and ERCOT, predicting outages at 92% accuracy, cutting unplanned downtime to 2.9% and saving $18 million in Q2. Renewables saw 15% turbine O&M drops via drones and IoT at Prairie Wind Farm, and robotic cleaning boosted Southwest solar by 3%. ERCOT heat waves kept gas at 95% factors.

Supply chain via Apex Supply Alliance consolidated 70% of $350 million parts spend, saving $12 million or 11%, with FGD optimizations on 1 GW coal saving $5 million. PJM coal phase-outs reallocated $15 million to storage.

Workforce via Apex Efficiency Academy and Oracle software cut overtime 28% to $8 million, storm costs 35% in Northeast, improving SAIDI to 85 minutes.

Regionally, ERCOT O&M per MWh fell 14% to $22 amid 12% demand growth; PJM 7% down; MISO 10% lift. We're ahead of peers at 9% deleveraging, renewables at 35% of fleet O&M. PowerSmart 2030 targets 15% reductions by 2030 to fund $3 billion clean capex at 10-12% ROE, with regulatory trackers recovering 60%.

Our balance sheet is strong with $4.2 billion liquidity, 3.2x net debt-to-EBITDA. We repurchased $200 million shares and raised dividends 5% to $0.48/share.

On rate base growth outlook, our $52.4 billion regulated rate base grew at 7.2% CAGR over five years from $38.7 billion via $18.5 billion capex. We project $72-75 billion by 2028 at 7-8% CAGR, adding $22 billion net from $4.8-5.2 billion annual capex. Bridge: $15 billion organic, $4.5 billion AFUDC, $1.5 billion CWIP, $0.5-1 billion M&A, less $2-3 billion depreciation.

Drivers: T&D $2.2 billion yearly for $10 billion program, including $3.5 billion reconductoring and PJM RTEP share. Generation $1.5 billion for 4 GW renewables/storage, retiring 1.8 GW coal for H-class gas. Load growth $700 million for 5 GW data centers and 250,000 EV chargers. Regulatory assumes 9.8-10.2% ROE, CWIP on 70%.

Assumptions: 1.8-2.2% load CAGR, 95% capex in-service, 80-90% ROE recovery. Risks: ROE variance or FERC delays.

For earnings guidance next quarter and full year, Q4 2024 adjusted EPS $1.85-2.05, up 12% YoY midpoint from Q3's $1.72. Revenues $2.85-3.05 billion, EBITDA $950 million-$1.05 billion at 34% margins. Regulated EBITDA $520-560 million on rate base and 2.5% residential/5% commercial growth. Competitive $430-490 million on $28-32/MWh spark spreads, 85% wind dispatch. Tailwinds: 1.2 GW hyperscaler PPAs, 300 MW ERCOT BESS, $50 million nuclear AFUDC. Pressures: $3.50-4.00 gas, MISO OATT hikes.

Full-year 2024 raised: EPS $7.40-7.80 up 10% from 2023's $6.95; revenues $11.8-12.4 billion; EBITDA $3.85-4.15 billion. YTD beats from 3% load, auction wins, $400 million capex under budget.

2025 initial: EPS $8.00-8.60 (14% growth); revenues $12.5-13.3 billion; EBITDA $4.2-4.6 billion on IRA credits, nuclear PTCs, Reliable Renewables pivot to 40% carbon-free. Capex $3.0 billion: T&D 40%, clean gen 35%, AMI 25%. Risks: mild winters, MOPR changes.

Regarding forward-looking statements and implications, as noted earlier, these involve risks like gas/power volatility in ERCOT/PJM, FERC changes, supply disruptions, weather, rates on $12.5 billion debt, cyber threats, IRA shifts. See our filings.

For 2025, EPS $4.85-5.15 (6-9% growth), EBITDA $2.85-3.05 billion on 12% Texas/Southeast load, $2.4-2.6 billion capex. To 2030, 7-9% EBITDA CAGR to $4.2-4.6 billion, renewables/storage to 65% of 18 GW fleet. Initiatives: $250 million SMRs with NuScale, CCUS/hydrogen blending, DERMS VPPs. ERCOT 55% EBITDA on tight margins; PJM auctions; Southeast gas/nuclear; West arbitrage. Delivers 10% TSR, 6-8% dividends.

We remain committed to a strong balance sheet and shareholder returns. We anticipate continued AFFO growth of 6-8%.

David Chen: Thank you, Maria. On operations, we're seeing improved efficiency in our CCGT power plants due to AI predictive maintenance and digital twins. This has resulted in a 15% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 22 basis points to 2.9%.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, David. For long-term strategy, we're exploring battery storage and hydrogen in ERCOT. This will drive growth. We're evaluating acquisitions in the Midwest market.

Robert Kim: Thank you, Lisa. Technologically, investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity include deploying advanced intrusion detection systems to counter threats. We're piloting dynamic line ratings in PJM.

Emily Torres: Thank you, Robert. Regulatorily, we received approval for our rate case filing in PJM. This allows 10.2% ROE recovery on new capex.

John Harlan: Thank you, Maria, David, Lisa, Robert, and Emily. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Mike Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Thompson: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for renewable portfolio growth?

John Harlan: Certainly. We're adding 1.2 GW next year, including solar-BESS hybrids and onshore wind, backed by PPAs with hyperscalers. This supports our 40% carbon-free target by 2027, with IRRs above 12% post-IRA.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jennifer Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jennifer Lee: What is your outlook for earnings guidance amid gas volatility?

Maria Gonzalez: Our Q4 and full-year ranges incorporate $3.25-3.75 gas, with 85% hedged. Raised midpoints reflect load beats and capex efficiency, positioning for 14% 2025 growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Tom Rivera: How are you mitigating risks related to supply chain disruptions?

David Chen: We've built 90-day buffers, long-term contracts with GE Vernova and Siemens, and vendor consolidation saving 11%. Digital tools predict issues early, keeping us ahead.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Greenlight Capital. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks. Can you walk us through your retirement of fossil fuel plants and replacement strategies?

Maria Gonzalez: Thanks, Sarah. Our legacy fossil fleet is 35% of 25,000 MW capacity, down from 52% five years ago—8,750 MW thermal, mostly 6,200 MW coal in Midwest/PJM. Capacity factors fell to 45% from 70% due to cheap renewables, $2.50 gas, RPS/CSAPR. Last year, retired 1,800 MW at River Bend/Oakridge, cutting $220 million O&M, $180 million impairment offset by $120 million salvage.

By 2026, another 2,500 MW: 1,200 MW MISO coal, 1,300 MW ERCOT peakers. $4.2 billion capex to 2028 replaces with 60% renewables (2,400 MW)—Buckeye Solar 450 MWdc/150 MW BESS at $28/MWh LCOE, 55% firmed factor, $65/MWh peaks, 80% PPAs. Horizon Wind 1,000 MW Vestas at 35% factors, PTCs. 1,200 MW/4,800 MWh storage for CAISO arbitrage at 12% IRR, iron-air pilots.

25% efficient gas—1,000 MW 7HA.02 H-class at 64%, CCS-ready, hydrogen trials. 15% nuclear—$800 million extensions for +15% output, NuScale SMRs by 2029.

Regional: PJM RGGI solar-storage for auctions; ERCOT gas for Uri risks; CAISO storage. EPS lift $0.12 last year, $0.45 by 2026, 9.5% ROIC. Hedged supply, $200 million deposits. Divested non-core, rates up 2.8% YoY.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to John Harlan for closing remarks.

John Harlan: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Apex Power Generation for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Apex Power Generation.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
